visual: Low, mound-forming Japanese maple with cascading branches and very finely divided, feathery green leaves that develop vivid yellow, orange and red autumn colour. Small purplish-red flowers in spring are followed by red winged fruits.
water: Moderate; keep evenly moist while establishing and water during prolonged dry summer weather.
soilWarning: No waterlogging, drought or drying winds
prune: Minimal pruning required; remove dead, damaged or crossing growth between late autumn and midwinter.
hardinessNote: −20 to −15°C · hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
resilience: Excellent cold tolerance but benefits from shelter from strong, drying winds and reliable summer moisture.
uses: Specimen shrub, Japanese gardens, courtyard gardens, rock gardens, banks, slopes and large containers.
uncertain: The name 'Acer palmatum dissectum' can also be used loosely for the wider Dissectum Group of laceleaf Japanese maples. RHS separately accepts Acer palmatum 'Dissectum' as a named plant, so this entry uses that identity.
If the plant has red or purple foliage rather than green foliage, it may belong to a different cultivar within the Dissectum Group.
